title: Choose the CAHMA Control visual world
question: Both leading directions preserve the live camera system and restrained industrial brief. Choose the operating language that should govern the build.

options.label: Optical Metrology Bench
options.lineage: machine-vision calibration stations and optical inspection instruments
options.thesis: Treat every feed as a measured specimen and every dispatch as a traceable instrument reading.
options.viewport: A dominant measured camera field anchors the left side while a fixed instrumentation rail reports dispatch, capacity, model state, and alarms; secondary feeds and ranked candidates remain visible below.
options.risk: If the measurement grammar is applied too literally, overlays could compete with the camera imagery.

raised.raise: One consistent measurement coordinate system adapts across every feed and viewport without imitating a terminal.
Recent dispatches form a persistent, readable frame sequence instead of disappearing after each decision.
Connection and scheduler phases are discrete, named states rather than color-only ambience.
Every region is named literally; unavailable areas receive an explicit structural mark rather than decorative chrome.
The selected feed gains real scale while the other feeds remain visible and legible.
Camera imagery, inference overlays, policy, and routing are separate layers with a stable legend.

options.label: Broadcast Engineering Multiviewer
options.lineage: broadcast master-control rooms and professional camera multiviewers
options.thesis: Make live feeds the wall and let routing, tally, timing, and alarms behave like broadcast engineering signals.
options.viewport: A disciplined asymmetric multiview puts the active feed first, keeps all cameras live, and places scheduler and resource telemetry in an engineering sidecar.
options.risk: This is the strongest familiar solution, but it can look like a conventional surveillance wall unless CAHMA's policy-first scheduler remains dominant.

options.label: Glyph Scene
options.thesis: Translate camera luminance into one character-grid instrumentation surface.
options.viewport: Every camera becomes a live glyph-density view with metrics embedded in the same grid.
options.case: It commits to one coherent coordinate system but obscures real video evidence and conflicts with the ban on terminal aesthetics.
options.risk: The interface would read as a technical novelty instead of a credible camera operation.
options.kept: A single adaptive measurement grid governs all live regions.

options.label: Dispatch Cutting Bench
options.lineage: film cutting benches and perforated select rails
options.thesis: Represent scheduler decisions as selected frames on a persistent editorial rail.
options.viewport: Feeds sit on a horizontal decision strip with the selected dispatch marked as the current frame.
options.case: The temporal metaphor is useful, but a scrub rail weakens simultaneous system monitoring and camera comparison.
options.risk: It prioritizes history over present operational state.
options.kept: Recent decisions remain visible as a persistent sequence.

options.label: Scheduler Cue Bands
options.thesis: Organize the scheduler into named phases that move from observation to protected inference.
options.viewport: System state appears as stacked atmospheric phases tied to a cue timeline.
options.case: Named phases clarify state, but the source relies on gradient atmosphere that the brief explicitly prohibits.
options.kept: Every runtime phase has a discrete label and non-color indicator.

options.label: Quoted Stockroom
options.lineage: industrial streetwear labeling and warehouse tags
options.thesis: Name every operational zone literally and mark selected state with attached physical tags.
options.viewport: Feeds and resources become hard-labeled stockroom zones with the active route tagged in orange.
options.case: Literal labeling supports comprehension, but repeated quotation and hazard stripes become decoration and violate the restrained brief.
options.risk: The fashion reference could overwhelm the engineering content.
options.kept: Labels use direct operational nouns and unavailable regions receive unmistakable structure.

options.label: Focused Camera Catalog
options.thesis: Let the active camera expand while surrounding feeds step back.
options.viewport: Camera rows expand the selected feed and reveal its operational metadata on focus.
options.case: Feed prominence is useful, but hiding metadata until focus is inappropriate for continuous monitoring.
options.risk: The system would feel like media browsing rather than operations.
options.kept: Selection changes scale without removing awareness of other cameras.

options.label: Routing Map Legend
options.thesis: Separate fixed camera terrain from a live scheduler route drawn above it.
options.viewport: The policy layer stays fixed beneath a numbered live route through camera and model controls.
options.case: Layer separation is excellent, but geographic map semantics and multi-ink color reduce product clarity for a non-spatial scheduler.
options.risk: Judges could mistake routing for camera geography.
options.kept: Base state and live decision overlays remain independently legible.

canonCard.label: Standard dark operations dashboard
canonCard.thesis: A familiar dark admin shell with camera cards, KPI tiles, and charts.
canonCard.viewport: A conventional header, KPI row, equal camera cards, and lower monitoring panels.
canonCard.risk: Immediately understandable but largely indistinguishable from generic monitoring software.
